lens: Tailwind Plus Catalyst application shell: sidebar layout, refined defaults, fast to build
name: Live Desk Cockpit
one_liner: A Catalyst-style sidebar app shell built from MIT parts, a dark-first live cockpit that coaches and scores every turn, and a persona catalogue with a Codex-checked contributor path.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Catalyst lens: persistent desktop sidebar, stacked mobile navigation, clean page headers and description lists, and copy-in components for fast builds. Changed one thing: Catalyst's source ships under the Tailwind Plus licence (Tailwind's blog says it comes with a Tailwind UI all-access licence), so it cannot be committed to an MIT repo. I kept the pattern and used MIT parts instead (shadcn/ui, cmdk, Motion, Recharts). Research: 3 Mobbin searches (live call, persona library, creation wizard) and 2 Firecrawl searches of competitor pages (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Outdoo, Yoodli). The Catalyst page scrape returned 404, so the licence point rests on Tailwind's own blog text. Self-scored: A 8, B 7, C 7, D 5.6 (conditional), E 5.3 (conditional), F1 6, F2 7, F3 3.

design_language.typography: Geist (OFL, via next/font/google) for UI and headings, 600 weight with -0.02em tracking on H1 and H2. Geist Mono with tabular numerals for timers, scores, rubric weights and transcript timestamps. Body 15px over 1.6 on desktop and 16px on mobile. Replaces Sora and Inter.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radius 10px on controls, 14px on cards, 20px on sheets. Hairline 1px borders carry most of the structure; one soft elevation only on floating cue cards. Cockpit surfaces are flat dark panels, and signal glow appears only on the active coach state.
design_language.motion: Cue cards slide in over 180ms with ease-out and stack, three visible at most. Rubric meters tween over 400ms when status changes. The presence ring pulses only while the persona speaks. Everything drops to fades under prefers-reduced-motion.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.5px stroke, always beside a text label on mobile. Fixed cue icons: ear for whisper, target for objection, route for talk track, gauge for pace. No emoji anywhere in the UI.
design_language.theme_modes: Light by default for library, pre-call, debrief, dashboard and manager views. Dark by default for the live cockpit and the landing hero. Both follow prefers-color-scheme with a toggle in the top bar, and every token has a dark value.

navigation_and_ia: Desktop uses a persistent left sidebar with five groups: Practice (Pre-call, Live call), Library (Personas, Scenarios, New with AI), Progress (Dashboard, History), Team (Manager view, shown only inside an org), and Settings (Rubrics, Models and cost, Security). The top bar holds Cmd-K, Start call and the theme toggle. Between 1024 and 1279px the sidebar collapses to icons. Below 768px it becomes a four-item bottom tab bar with a More sheet. The live call uses focus mode: sidebar hidden, a 48px call bar with timer, mute and End. Existing routes (/trainer, /trainer/scenarios, /trainer/debrief/[id], /dashboard, /settings/security) keep their paths so links and tests survive.

live_coaching_and_scoring: A three-zone cockpit: persona and talk track on the left, call stage in the centre, coach rail on the right. After every rep turn a GPT-4.1-mini structured-output call returns per-criterion status (not started, partial, covered), one evidence line and up to two cues. It is debounced so it never blocks the voice path. Cue types: whisper (next best question), objection alert (detected objection plus a suggested reply), talk-track progress (steps tick off), and pace (talk ratio). Cues go only to the rep and never to the persona or the audio channel. When the grader is unavailable the rail shows a grey Heuristic badge instead of a score, matching the banner the debrief shows today. The debrief reuses the same criteria, with each quote linked to its transcript line and a Replay this moment action.
persona_library_and_wizard: The library is a catalogue organised by job family: SDR cold call, AE discovery, insurance, mortgage, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success and collections. Each family is a horizontal shelf plus a full grid. A left filter rail covers role, industry, difficulty, objection type, channel and length. Cards show the persona, a one-line goal, objection chips and a CI-checked badge when the pack passes schema and rubric-sum checks. Launch target: 120 personas and 60 scenarios, all JSON validated. New with AI opens the wizard: one prompt box with source chips (job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP, pasted call), numbered clarifying choice cards with Skip, a stepper covering persona, objections, rubric and voice, a 60-second test call, then save privately or open a PR with the pack.
signature_moments: A whisper cue appears in the coach rail the moment the persona says Nobody mentioned a fee, with the exact line to say.
Rubric meters fill live, and a criterion turns to covered only when a quote backs it.
Replay this moment in the debrief drops the rep back at the turn they fumbled, with the same persona state.
Every wizard field carries a provenance chip that points to the source sentence it came from.
The landing hero is the live cockpit itself, not a stock illustration.
Library cards carry a CI-checked badge, so contributors see that their pack passed validation.
openai_fund_angle: Show the models on screen. The cockpit has a Models chip row, and Settings > Models lists each model with its job (persona text, per-turn scoring, debrief, wizard generation) and a per-call cost estimate. Add OpenAI Realtime as a selectable voice engine beside ElevenLabs. Make contribution the front door: a Build a persona with Codex page produces a schema-valid JSON pack from a form, and the repo's PR workflow uses Codex in PR review to check the schema, rubric weights summing to 100, objection coverage and tone, then posts the result as a review comment. The README hero shows a 15-second live-coaching clip, a Built with OpenAI line and links to each model's docs. Good-first-persona issues are labelled for new contributors.

implementation.migration_path: 1) Add CSS-variable tokens (light and dark), Geist fonts and shadcn Button, Card, Tabs, Sheet and Dialog; swap .card and .btn-primary usages. 2) Build AppShell and mount /trainer, /dashboard and /trainer/debrief under it. 3) Rebuild pre-call and debrief first, since they need no engine change. 4) Add per-turn structured scoring and the coach rail behind a flag; keep the voice and text paths untouched. 5) Move scenarios to schema-validated JSON packs, ship the catalogue and the CI check, then the wizard endpoint. 6) Manager view behind an org flag. Each step ships on its own; the live cockpit is the only step that changes the engine.

risks: Catalyst cannot be committed to an MIT repo. This proposal swaps it for MIT parts. If the owner insists on Catalyst code, it has to stay out of the public repo.
Per-turn scoring adds latency and cost on every turn. Debounce, cap cues per turn, and show the Heuristic or pending badge rather than a stale score.
Cues must never reach the persona or the audio channel. Enforce this in the prompt and the transport, and test it.
Content quality: 120 GPT-written personas need human review before launch. CI catches schema and weight errors, not realism.
Competitor claims come from vendor blogs (Second Nature, Hyperbound, Outdoo) and are unverified. Do not repeat them in the README.
Dropping the orb and the in-call three.js visuals lowers the wow factor on the live screen. Keep R3F only on the lazy-loaded landing hero.
Dark cockpit plus light pages doubles QA. Amber and teal text on dark must be checked against WCAG AA.
Voice calls and team views need recording-consent notices, and reps must consent before managers see individual scores.
Self-scores D 5.6 and E 5.3 are conditional on per-turn scoring shipping and on at least 100 reviewed personas. Without both, they fall below 5.0.
